confirmed: The complete markdown, including references and supplement, was read; the local PDF has 55 pages and no printed manuscript date or version number. The form's description as an undated OSF manuscript with appended supplement is supported (PDF p. 1; pp. 49-55; retrieval record for provenance).
The title and all named authors match the document (PDF p. 1).

One non-randomized study used the fixed initial-idea, AI-evaluation, second-idea sequence in both existing student cohorts; only problem-topic presentation order was randomized. quasi_people, observational context, core=no, and has_randomized_people_study=false are supported (PDF pp. 12-15, Sections 3.1-3.2.2; p. 33, Section 5.3).

The reported retained people counts are 99 engineering students and 212 psychology students, totaling 311 after participant exclusions; no AI-assignment count is reported, and this is not a study with fewer than 50 retained people (PDF p. 12, Section 3.1).
The task involved four engineering design problems, and the entire study took approximately 45 minutes (PDF p. 12, Section 3.1; p. 14, Section 3.2.2 and Table 1).

GPT-3.5-turbo ideas were generated before the study and kept consistent across participants; six were selected per problem. Water Access had five unique solutions because one was shown twice (PDF p. 11, Section 2; pp. 15-16, Section 3.2.3; p. 52, Supplemental Table 1 note).

Originality and effectiveness are automated AIDE scores on participant-generated solutions, and Table 3 reports Z-scored AIDE ratings; these are eligible output measures rather than self-reported creativity (PDF p. 17, Section 3.3.1; p. 21, Table 3 note).
S1-O1 correctly reports originality t(1209)=-7.04, p<.001, and Wilcoxon signed-rank W=233232, p<.001 (PDF p. 20, Section 4.2; p. 21, text below Table 3).
S1-O1 means and SDs match Table 3: engineering Idea 1 0.371 (0.884), Idea 2 0.480 (0.897); psychology Idea 1 -0.255 (1.000), Idea 2 -0.042 (0.635) (PDF p. 21, Table 3).
S1-O2 correctly reports effectiveness t(1209)=-7.84, p<.001, and Wilcoxon signed-rank W=248292, p<.001 (PDF p. 20, Section 4.2; p. 21, text below Table 3).
S1-O2 means and SDs match Table 3: engineering Idea 1 0.003 (0.975), Idea 2 0.247 (0.941); psychology Idea 1 -0.075 (0.938), Idea 2 0.127 (0.848) (PDF p. 21, Table 3).

The form correctly flags an unresolved unit inconsistency for the creativity tests: the methods say scores were averaged across four problems, but the paired tests print 1209 degrees of freedom despite 311 retained people. Leaving their analysis unit unresolved is justified by this source (PDF p. 12, Section 3.1; pp. 18-19, Sections 3.3.1 and 3.4; p. 20, Section 4.2).

S1-O3 correctly describes six human-coded inspiration categories and reports chi-square(5, N = 1210) = 28.60, p < .001. Completely New Idea is engineering 60 (15.5%) versus psychology 71 (8.6%); Direct Adoption of AI Idea is 22 (5.6%) versus 93 (11.3%) (PDF p. 18, Section 3.3.3; p. 26, Table 6; p. 27, Section 4.5).
Idea inspiration compares each second idea with that participant's initial idea and the supplied AI ideas; it is not a diversity comparison across different people (PDF p. 18, Section 3.3.3).

The one-line finding's sample count and test statistics match the PDF, and its caution about practice effects matches the authors' explicit acknowledgment that there is no control group (PDF p. 12, Section 3.1; p. 20, Section 4.2; p. 33, Section 5.3).

The appended supplement contains AI ideas and AIDE ratings, problem-level descriptive statistics, alternative models using raw self-evaluations, and a correlation matrix, as the form states (PDF pp. 49-52, Supplemental Table 1; pp. 52-53, Supplemental Table 2; pp. 53-54, Supplemental Tables 3-4; p. 55, Supplemental Figure 1).
This is an original study rather than a synthesis, so there are no pooled estimates or synthesis study counts to extract (PDF pp. 12-19, Method and Analysis; pp. 20-28, Results).
summary: The source supports a non-randomized before/after study of 311 retained students, classified as quasi_people and observational context, with no randomized AI-assistance study. All reported numerical results and the one-line finding match the PDF, but exclusions, the coded-output count, outcome/contrast metadata, and data/code links need completion.
